title: Black Sea shipping, a shark die-off and kerbside EV chargers

stories.headline: Türkiye urges Russia and Ukraine to stop Black Sea shipping attacks
stories.headlineZh: 土耳其敦促俄乌停止袭击黑海船只
stories.summaryZh: 埃尔多安与泽连斯基在伊斯坦布尔会面，同意推动新的黑海粮食走廊，美国也关注有限停火方案。
stories.c1:
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan has called on both Russia and Ukraine to stop attacking civilian vessels in the Black Sea, a waterway that remains vital to global food and energy supplies. Speaking at a joint news conference in Istanbul on Saturday alongside Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, he insisted that such strikes were unacceptable under any circumstances and urged all parties to act responsibly. The two leaders also agreed to work towards a new corridor for grain shipments through the sea.

Türkiye occupies an unusual position in the conflict, maintaining working relationships with both Moscow and Kyiv, and it has grown increasingly frustrated by attacks on commercial shipping. Ankara has sent both sides a proposal to halt the strikes, although neither has yet acted on it. The risks were underlined on 28 October, when a Liberian-flagged container ship was hit by drones in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone.

The diplomatic push appears to be gathering momentum beyond the region. On the same day, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there was growing international interest in a limited ceasefire at sea to protect grain and energy shipments, adding that Washington was reviewing proposals from Türkiye and India. He was candid about the limits of such a deal: "It doesn't solve the war, but at least it solves a unique aspect of it."

Erdogan argued that an agreement on safe navigation could give fresh impetus to broader peace efforts, while Zelenskyy stressed that strong decisions would be needed to end the fighting. According to the Kremlin, the next round of talks between Russia, Ukraine and the United States is expected to take place in the United Arab Emirates this month. Whether a narrow maritime arrangement can pave the way for something more ambitious, however, remains far from certain.
stories.b2:
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan has asked Russia and Ukraine to stop attacking civilian ships in the Black Sea. The sea is very important for moving food and energy around the world. Erdogan spoke at a news conference in Istanbul on Saturday with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. He said the attacks could not be accepted, and the two leaders agreed to work on a new route for grain ships.

Türkiye has good relations with both Moscow and Kyiv, and it is unhappy about attacks on commercial ships. It has sent both countries a plan to stop the attacks, but neither has acted on it yet. On 28 October, drones hit a container ship in waters belonging to Bulgaria.

On the same day, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said more countries were interested in a limited ceasefire at sea to protect grain and energy shipments. He said the United States was studying plans from Türkiye and India. He admitted that such a deal would not end the war.

Erdogan said an agreement on safe shipping could help wider peace efforts. The Kremlin says the next talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US should happen in the United Arab Emirates this month. It is not clear yet whether a small deal at sea can lead to something bigger.

vocab.en: to formally ask someone to do something
vocab.example: The council has called on residents to save water during the heatwave.

vocab.en: in any situation at all (usually used with a negative)
vocab.example: Staff must not share their passwords under any circumstances.

vocab.en: to make efforts to achieve a goal over time
vocab.example: Our team is working towards a fully paperless office by next year.

vocab.en: to become more and more annoyed because something is not improving
vocab.example: Commuters have grown increasingly frustrated with the constant train delays.

vocab.en: to show clearly that something is important or true
vocab.example: The outage underlined how much we depend on a single supplier.

vocab.en: to develop and become stronger or faster
vocab.example: The campaign for a four-day week is slowly gathering momentum.

vocab.en: to speak honestly and openly about something
vocab.example: The manager was candid about the risks of launching so early.

vocab.en: to provide new energy or encouragement for something
vocab.example: The new funding could give fresh impetus to cancer research.

vocab.en: to create the conditions that make something possible
vocab.example: The pilot program could pave the way for a national rollout.

questions.q: Erdogan and Zelenskyy held their joint news conference in Ankara.
questions.explain: 原文说 "Speaking at a joint news conference in Istanbul"，地点是伊斯坦布尔而非安卡拉，因此为 False。

questions.q: Neither Russia nor Ukraine has yet acted on Türkiye's proposal to halt the strikes.
questions.explain: 原文明确写道 "neither has yet acted on it"，与题干一致，因此为 True。

questions.q: India has offered to send naval vessels to escort grain ships.
questions.explain: 原文只提到美国正在审议 "proposals from Türkiye and India"，并未说明印度提出派遣军舰护航，因此为 Not Given。

questions.q: What did Marco Rubio suggest about a limited ceasefire at sea?
options: It would bring the war to a quick end.
It would deal with only one part of the conflict.
The United States had already rejected the idea.
Only Türkiye was interested in it.
questions.explain: Rubio 说 "It doesn't solve the war, but at least it solves a unique aspect of it"，即只能解决战争的一个方面，故选 B。

stories.discuss: Why do you think limited agreements, such as protecting shipping routes, are sometimes easier to reach than a full peace deal? Can they really lead to lasting peace?

stories.headline: Algal bloom killed more than 8,000 sharks and rays in South Australia
stories.headlineZh: 南澳有毒藻华致逾八千条鲨鱼和鳐鱼死亡
stories.summaryZh: 基于公民科学数据的新报告显示，南澳藻华可能造成有记录以来最大规模的鲨鳐死亡事件。
stories.c1:
South Australia's toxic algal bloom may have caused the largest mass die-off of sharks and rays ever recorded. A new report, drawing on thousands of observations logged by citizen scientists and compiled by the Great Southern Reef Foundation, found that more than 8,000 of these animals washed up dead along the state's coast. Among them were roughly 4,500 southern fiddler rays, 850 Port Jackson sharks and 670 wobbegongs, and because many deaths would have gone unreported, the true toll is almost certainly higher.

For Charlie Huveneers, a professor at Flinders University, the figures are sobering. His own tagging research offers little comfort: of the more than 150 sharks and rays he had tagged before the bloom, not a single one had returned a year later. Since these species mature slowly, breed infrequently and produce small litters, he expects any recovery to be painfully slow, although animals from unaffected areas may eventually move in.

The report also warns that some local populations may have collapsed. Particular concern surrounds two rare species with very small ranges that overlap heavily with the bloom: the pygmy thornback skate and the coastal stingaree, which is listed as endangered internationally. Neither, however, is listed as threatened by the federal government, and the environment department points to insufficient data on their population status.

Veteran diver David Muirhead, who has completed around 2,000 dives in the state's waters, has noticed many common fish and invertebrates bouncing back. Rays are another matter: he has spotted only one since the bloom. Having photographed a pygmy thornback skate early on, he admits he may have been "witnessing, perhaps, the end of one species."
stories.b2:
South Australia's toxic algal bloom may have killed more sharks and rays than any event ever recorded. A new report used thousands of records from citizen scientists, collected by the Great Southern Reef Foundation. It found that more than 8,000 sharks and rays washed up dead on the coast. They included about 4,500 southern fiddler rays, 850 Port Jackson sharks and 670 wobbegongs. Many deaths were never reported, so the real number is probably higher.

Charlie Huveneers, a professor at Flinders University, tagged more than 150 sharks and rays before the bloom. A year later, none of them had come back. These animals grow up slowly and have few young, so he thinks recovery will take a long time.

The report says some local populations may have disappeared. Experts are especially worried about two rare species, the pygmy thornback skate and the coastal stingaree, which live mainly in the affected area. The federal government does not list either species as threatened, saying there is not enough data.

Diver David Muirhead has made about 2,000 dives in the state's waters. He says many common fish are returning, but he has seen only one ray since the bloom.

vocab.en: to use information or experience as a source
vocab.example: The novel draws on the author's childhood in country Victoria.

vocab.en: the real number of deaths or amount of damage
vocab.example: Officials warned that the true toll of the floods may never be known.

vocab.en: making you feel serious and think carefully
vocab.example: It's a sobering thought that half the reef has been bleached.

vocab.en: to do little to make a worrying situation feel better
vocab.example: The small pay rise offers little comfort to renters facing higher costs.

vocab.en: so slow that it is frustrating or worrying
vocab.example: Progress on the new train line has been painfully slow.

vocab.en: to cover part of the same area or time as something else
vocab.example: My shift overlaps with yours on Thursday afternoons.

vocab.en: not enough for a particular purpose
vocab.example: The judge ruled that there was insufficient evidence to proceed.

vocab.en: to recover quickly after a difficult period
vocab.example: Local tourism bounced back faster than anyone expected.

vocab.en: used to say something is quite different or harder
vocab.example: Writing the report is easy; getting everyone to read it is another matter.

questions.q: The report's figure of more than 8,000 dead sharks and rays is likely to underestimate the real number.
questions.explain: 原文说 "because many deaths would have gone unreported, the true toll is almost certainly higher"，说明真实数字更高，因此为 True。

questions.q: Several of the sharks and rays tagged by Huveneers before the bloom were later detected again.
questions.explain: 原文说 "not a single one had returned a year later"，与题干相反，因此为 False。

questions.q: The algal bloom first appeared after an unusually hot summer.
questions.explain: 原文没有提到藻华出现的原因或时间（如 "hot summer"），因此为 Not Given。

questions.q: Why does Huveneers expect recovery to be slow?
options: Because the water is still toxic.
Because fishing in the area has increased.
Because these species mature slowly and have few young.
Because no animals live in nearby unaffected areas.
questions.explain: 原文说这些物种 "mature slowly, breed infrequently and produce small litters"，所以恢复缓慢，故选 C。

stories.discuss: Why do you think ordinary people are increasingly involved in collecting scientific data? What are the strengths and weaknesses of relying on citizen science?

stories.headline: Thousands of kerbside EV chargers may sit idle without dedicated parking
stories.headlineZh: 缺少专用车位，数千个路边电动车充电桩或遭闲置
stories.summaryZh: 澳政府计划在电线杆上安装约1.4万个充电桩，但数据显示无专用车位的充电桩使用率极低。
stories.c1:
From 2027, the federal government plans to bolt about 14,000 electric vehicle chargers onto power poles in densely populated urban areas, where many residents have nowhere to charge at home. On paper, the Accelerating EV Charging Program makes sense: roughly a quarter of motorists lack off-street parking. Yet an ABC investigation suggests that a large share of these chargers could end up barely used, because most will not come with parking reserved for electric cars.

The evidence from Sydney's eastern suburbs is striking. A dedicated charger on Ocean Street in North Bondi recorded 988 sessions in a year, whereas an undedicated one on a nearby street managed just 40, and another in Bondi only four. Anthony Weinberg, who runs the charging program for three local councils, estimates that undedicated spots are used at just 5 to 10 per cent of the rate of dedicated ones, and his councils now refuse to install chargers without dedicated parking.

This raises awkward questions about the program's projected benefits. The government's modelling assumes each charger will support 30 electric vehicles, but industry analyst Ross de Rango found that undedicated chargers in the area supported about three, implying the forecasts could be out by a factor of ten. He also predicts disputes, warning that people can "absolutely expect grief over who gets to park."

Even the energy market regulator found only limited reliable evidence that such chargers boost uptake, although it concluded that the likely benefits still outweigh the costs to consumers, estimated at up to $1.44 per household a year. For its part, the climate change department says it expects a mix of site types and that usage will grow as more drivers go electric.
stories.b2:
From 2027, the federal government plans to put about 14,000 electric vehicle chargers on power poles in busy city areas. Many people there cannot charge at home, and about a quarter of drivers have no off-street parking. But an ABC investigation suggests that many of the new chargers may hardly be used, because most will not have parking spaces just for electric cars.

Data from Sydney's eastern suburbs shows the problem. A charger with its own parking space in North Bondi was used 988 times in a year. A charger without a special space on a nearby street was used only 40 times. Local councils there now refuse to install chargers without dedicated parking.

This matters for the government's plans. Its modelling expects each charger to support 30 electric cars. However, analyst Ross de Rango found that chargers without dedicated spaces supported only about three. He also expects arguments about parking.

The energy market regulator said there was limited evidence that these chargers help more people buy electric cars, but it still supports the plan. The cost could be up to $1.44 per household each year. The government says use will grow as more people switch to electric cars.

vocab.en: in theory, though perhaps not in reality
vocab.example: On paper, the new timetable looks faster, but trains are still late.

vocab.en: to finally be in a situation you did not plan
vocab.example: We ended up eating at home because every café was full.

vocab.en: a big part or proportion of something
vocab.example: A large share of the budget goes on rent.

vocab.en: very noticeable or unusual
vocab.example: There's a striking difference between the two survey results.

vocab.zh: 引发令人尴尬/棘手的问题
vocab.en: to make people ask difficult questions that are hard to answer
vocab.example: The leaked emails raise awkward questions for the company's board.

vocab.word: out by a factor of ten
vocab.en: wrong because the real figure is ten times bigger or smaller
vocab.example: Our early estimate was out by a factor of ten.

vocab.en: to increase the number of people who start using something
vocab.example: Free trials are a proven way to boost uptake of new apps.

vocab.en: to be greater or more important than something else
vocab.example: For most people, the benefits of exercise far outweigh the risks.

vocab.en: to switch to an electric vehicle or electric power
vocab.example: Rising petrol prices are pushing more families to go electric.

questions.q: About a quarter of motorists do not have off-street parking.
questions.explain: 原文说 "roughly a quarter of motorists lack off-street parking"，与题干一致，因此为 True。

questions.q: Weinberg's councils still install chargers without dedicated parking when funding is available.
questions.explain: 原文说 "his councils now refuse to install chargers without dedicated parking"，与题干相反，因此为 False。

questions.q: Most of the new chargers will be installed in regional towns.
questions.explain: 原文说充电桩将安装在 "densely populated urban areas"，即人口密集的城市地区，与题干相矛盾，因此为 False。

questions.q: What did Ross de Rango's analysis suggest?
options: The government's forecasts may be far too optimistic.
Undedicated chargers are used more than dedicated ones.
Each charger will support more than 30 vehicles.
Drivers prefer charging at petrol stations.
questions.explain: 他发现每个无专用车位的充电桩仅支持约三辆车，"the forecasts could be out by a factor of ten"，说明政府预测过于乐观，故选 A。

stories.discuss: Why do you think governments sometimes push ahead with plans even when the evidence is uncertain? Should public infrastructure wait until the evidence is clear?

stories.headline: More young men say violence for a cause can be justified
stories.headlineZh: 调查：更多年轻男性认为可为某种诉求诉诸暴力
stories.summaryZh: 麦金农指数显示，澳民众对政客信任下降，18至24岁男性中超过27%认为极端手段有时合理。
stories.c1:
A growing minority of young Australian men believe that violence can sometimes be justified to advance a cause, according to the second McKinnon Index, a survey of more than 4,000 people carried out with Roy Morgan in June and July. Among men aged 18 to 24, over 27 per cent said such "extreme measures" could occasionally be warranted, compared with about one in ten across the population as a whole. More than three-quarters of Australians rejected the idea outright.

The findings point to a broader sense of disillusionment among young men. Their support for democracy has slipped to 54 per cent, and the share who feel people can freely express political opinions has plummeted by 23 points to around half. Nationally, almost three-quarters believe the country has become more divided over the past year, and fewer than half feel the political system gives people like them a say.

The picture is not uniformly bleak, though. More than three-quarters of respondents still regard democracy as preferable to any other form of government, and trust in institutions has held up well even as faith in politicians has eroded. The Australian Electoral Commission is trusted by over 70 per cent of people, while courts and regulators also score comparatively well. Dissatisfaction runs highest in inner regional areas and among those with less formal education.

McKinnon's interim executive chairman, former Victorian deputy premier John Thwaites, described supporters of violence as a minority, albeit a growing one. Not everyone reads the results so gloomily, however. Political scientist Aaron Martin cautioned that two years of data make it hard to identify a genuine trend, pointing out that other research showed satisfaction with democracy rising between 2019 and 2025.
stories.b2:
A new survey suggests that more young Australian men now think violence can sometimes be acceptable to support a cause. The second McKinnon Index asked more than 4,000 people about democracy in June and July. More than 27 per cent of men aged 18 to 24 said "extreme measures" could sometimes be justified. Across the whole population, the figure was about one in ten.

Young men also seem less happy with the system. Only 54 per cent of them support democracy, and only about half think people can freely share political opinions. Almost three-quarters of all Australians think the country is more divided than a year ago.

However, there is some good news. More than three-quarters of people still think democracy is the best system of government. Trust in politicians has fallen, but trust in institutions has stayed fairly strong. More than 70 per cent of people trust the Australian Electoral Commission.

John Thwaites, the interim chair of the group behind the index, said people who support violence are a small but growing group. But political scientist Aaron Martin warned that two years of data are not enough to show a real trend.

vocab.en: a small group that is becoming bigger
vocab.example: A growing minority of workers now refuse to answer emails after hours.

vocab.en: necessary or reasonable in the circumstances
vocab.example: Given the storm warnings, cancelling the match was warranted.

vocab.en: to refuse completely and immediately
vocab.example: The union rejected the offer outright.

vocab.en: disappointment after discovering something is not as good as you believed
vocab.example: There's growing disillusionment with the promises of social media.

vocab.en: to fall suddenly and by a large amount
vocab.example: Ticket sales plummeted after the bad reviews came out.

vocab.en: to have the right to influence a decision
vocab.example: Tenants should have a say in how the building is managed.
forms: gives people like them a say

vocab.en: negative or depressing in every way
vocab.example: The forecast for the economy isn't uniformly bleak.

vocab.en: to remain strong or stable in a difficult situation
vocab.example: Consumer spending has held up surprisingly well this year.

vocab.en: although (used before a word or phrase, not a full clause)
vocab.example: The plan worked, albeit more slowly than we'd hoped.

questions.q: The survey was conducted in partnership with Roy Morgan.
questions.explain: 原文说调查 "carried out with Roy Morgan in June and July"，因此为 True。

questions.q: Most Australians now believe another system of government would be better than democracy.
questions.explain: 原文说 "More than three-quarters of respondents still regard democracy as preferable to any other form of government"，与题干相反，因此为 False。

questions.q: Young women were less likely than young men to support extreme measures.
questions.explain: 原文只给出年轻男性和全体人口的数据，没有提到年轻女性 ("young women")，因此为 Not Given。

questions.q: Why is Aaron Martin cautious about the results?
options: He thinks the sample was too small.
He believes only two years of data cannot show a real trend.
He says trust in the electoral commission is falling.
He doubts the survey questions were fair.
questions.explain: 原文说 Martin "cautioned that two years of data make it hard to identify a genuine trend"，故选 B。

stories.discuss: Why do you think some young people are losing faith in democracy? What could governments or communities do to rebuild their trust?

dialogue.title: The Office Cup Sweep
dialogue.titleZh: 办公室的墨尔本杯抽签
dialogue.setting: On the Monday before the Melbourne Cup, two colleagues chat in the office kitchen while waiting for the kettle to boil.
dialogue.settingZh: 墨尔本杯前一天（周一），两位同事在办公室茶水间等水烧开时闲聊。

lines.name: Priya
lines.en: Morning! Have you put your name down for the Cup sweep yet?
lines.zh: 早！你报名参加墨尔本杯的抽签了吗？

lines.name: Tom
lines.en: Not yet. Honestly, I wouldn't know one horse from another.
lines.zh: 还没。说实话，我根本分不清哪匹马是哪匹。

lines.name: Priya
lines.en: That's the beauty of it — you just draw a name out of a hat.
lines.zh: 这就是它的妙处——你只要从帽子里抽个名字就行。

lines.name: Tom
lines.en: Fair enough. How much are we chipping in this year?
lines.zh: 有道理。今年每人要凑多少钱？

lines.name: Priya
lines.en: Five bucks a ticket. Whoever draws the winner takes the lot.
lines.zh: 一张票五块钱。谁抽中冠军马，奖金全归谁。

lines.name: Tom
lines.en: Go on then, put me down for two. I'm feeling lucky.
lines.zh: 那好吧，给我记两张。我感觉今天运气不错。

lines.name: Priya
lines.en: Are you doing anything for the public holiday tomorrow?
lines.zh: 明天公众假期你有什么安排吗？

lines.name: Tom
lines.en: A few mates are having a barbie, so I'll probably watch the race there.
lines.zh: 几个朋友要办个烧烤，我大概会在那儿看比赛。

lines.name: Priya
lines.en: Sounds good. I'm planning to sleep in and keep a low profile.
lines.zh: 听起来不错。我打算睡个懒觉，低调地过一天。

lines.name: Tom
lines.en: Not one for dressing up and heading to Flemington, then?
lines.zh: 所以你不喜欢打扮一番去弗莱明顿赛马场？

lines.name: Priya
lines.en: I went once. The crowds were way too much for me, to be honest.
lines.zh: 我去过一次。说实话，人多得让我受不了。

lines.name: Tom
lines.en: I get that. Mind you, the fashion's half the fun for some people.
lines.zh: 我理解。不过话说回来，对有些人来说，看穿搭就占了一半乐趣。

lines.name: Priya
lines.en: True. Anyway, I'll let you know which horses you've drawn after lunch.
lines.zh: 没错。总之，午饭后我告诉你抽到了哪两匹马。

lines.name: Tom
lines.en: Cheers. If I win, the next round of coffees is on me.
lines.zh: 谢啦。如果我赢了，下一轮咖啡我请。

phrases.plain: I can't tell the horses apart.
phrases.en: I wouldn't know one horse from another

phrases.plain: That's the good thing about it.
How much money are we giving?
phrases.en: How much are we chipping in

phrases.plain: The winner gets all the money.
